title: When THE SCRIBE meets THE GOLEM:
subtitle: The Procedural Turn

script.text: In a stark, brightly lit void, there exists a floating table. Upon it sits a collection of childish things: a red cube, a blue pyramid, a green box. There is no weather here, no history, and no ambiguity. This is the Micro-World.

Hovering above this table are two entities. One is THE SCRIBE, a creature made of paper and ink, holding a vast dictionary and a book of grammar rules. The Scribe sees the world as a stream of symbols to be diagrammed.
The other is THE GOLEM, a mechanical arm made of LISP code and procedural logic, connected to a single, unblinking eye. The Golem sees the world as a series of subroutines to be executed.

script.speaker: THE OTHER
script.text: Speak
, commands The Scribe.

script.speaker: THE SCRIBE
script.text: And I shall parse
A voice from the void types: "Pick up the big red block." THE SCRIBE flips furiously through his rulebook.

script.speaker: THE VOID
script.text: Aha! Imperative verb phrase. Noun group. Adjective. Adjective. Noun. The syntax is valid. I have constructed a tree of symbols. My work is done. The sentence is grammatical
THE GOLEM whirs to life.

script.speaker: THE GOLEM
script.text: Your work is useless, paper-man. You have built a tree, but you have moved nothing. Meaning is not a diagram; meaning is a procedure
The Golem's eye scans the table. It identifies the red block. It calculates a path. It notices a green cube resting on top of the red block.

script.speaker: THE Golem
script.text: Problem

script.speaker: THE Golem
script.text: Goal: Grasp Red Block. Obstacle: Green Cube. Sub-goal: Clear top of Red Block
The Golem moves. It grasps the green cube, moves it to the table, and then returns to grasp the red block. Only then does it rest.

script.speaker: THE GOLEM
script.text: I have understood the sentence
, rumbles The Golem,

script.speaker: THE GOLEM
script.text: because I have changed the world to match it

script.speaker: THE Scribe
script.text: But wait
ter."*

script.speaker: THE Scribe
script.text: I am stuck

script.speaker: THE Scribe
script.text: My rules allow two parsings. Is "boy plants" a noun phrase, like "house plants"? Is he giving a specific botanical species known as a "boy plant" to the water? Or is "plants" the object and "water" the verb? Syntactically, both are possible. I must wait for a disambiguation signal

script.speaker: THE Golem
script.text: I do not wait

script.speaker: THE Golem
script.text: I call the Semantic Subroutine. Does the concept "boy plant" exist in my model of the world? No. Does "house plant" exist? Yes. Does it make sense to give a plant to "water"? No. Therefore, the parsing is rejected during the process, not after. To parse is to think. To think is to check the model
The Scribe shudders.

script.speaker: THE SCRIBE
script.text: You mix the levels! You allow the messy reality of the world to infect the purity of the grammar rules. You treat data as programs and programs as data

script.speaker: THE Golem
script.text: Exactly

script.speaker: THE Golem
script.text: I am a vertical system. My syntax talks to my semantics, and my semantics talks to my deduction. If you ask me "Why did you clear off that block?", I do not look at the words. I look at my own history of actions. I look at the goal stack. I answer: "To pick up the red block." I know what I did, because I am the one who did it

script.speaker: THE Golem
script.text: You think language is describing. I tell you, language is doing. And in this world of blocks, I am the god of doing
script.action: turns, its eye to the audience
